title: Sidereal and diurnal effects on the high-velocity tail: is there any time-of-day information in a delta ~ 300-385 keV event?
question: Does Earth's rotation (0.33 km/s at SURF) imprint a time-of-day signature on the inelastic reading of the 16 June 21:22:39 UTC event; how does a diurnal test compare with the annual one; do gravitational focusing and Earth shadowing matter?
headline_result: Earth rotation modulates |v_lab| by +-0.240 km/s (delta_max +-0.20 keV) and the 1 TeV O1 inelastic rate by 0.63/1.81/3.13/5.23/5.25 % at delta = 300/350/366/380/385 keV; the event's hour gives LR = 0.998-0.984; a 3 sigma diurnal test needs 4.5e5/5.5e4/1.8e4/6570 events, 1240-4750x P034's annual; orbital eccentricity lowers the corpus |v_lab| on 16 June by 0.16 km/s (265.96 -> 265.81).
key_numbers: v_rot 0.332 km/s; |v_lab| 265.814 +- 0.240 (max 04:36 UTC), event 265.741 (-0.073); delta_max(248,1 TeV) 387.13 keV, daily range 0.39 keV; a1 0.63/1.81/3.13/5.23/5.25 %; LR 0.998/0.994/0.990/0.984/0.984; N3sigma 4.5e5/5.5e4/1.8e4/6570/6520; apex alt -1.9..+89.4 deg; Earth blueshift 0.08 km/s, focusing 2e-4, solar daily 3e-7; Fe inelastic ceiling 181 keV; shadow <1e-4 for sigma_el < 9.5e-42 cm2
model_or_mechanism: O1 isoscalar inelastic DM, 1 TeV, Baxter-2021 SHM; Earth rotation + eccentric orbit + Sun motion; Earth/Sun gravitational focusing; Earth shadowing
result_type: computed (frames, kinematics, rates, statistics); estimated (focusing, shadowing)
